name: Beans
description: Rich in protein and iron. A staple in Rwandan diet. Can be mashed for young children or cooked as a stew.

name: Maize Porridge
description: Traditional porridge made from maize flour. Can be enriched with milk, groundnut paste, or mashed fruit for added nutrition.

name: Bananas
description: Widely available in Rwanda. Cooking bananas can be mashed for complementary feeding. Good source of energy.

name: Sweet Potatoes
description: Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes are rich in vitamin A. Can be boiled and mashed for young children.

name: Milk
description: Excellent source of calcium and protein. Can be added to porridge or given as a drink. Cow's milk available across Rwanda.

name: Eggs
description: Highly nutritious and easy to prepare. Boiled or scrambled eggs provide complete protein. Excellent for growing children.

name: Groundnuts
description: Energy-dense food rich in protein and healthy fats. Groundnut paste can be added to porridge to increase caloric density.

name: Green Vegetables
description: Dark green leafy vegetables like amaranth and spinach are rich in iron and vitamin A. Should be finely chopped for young children.

name: Sorghum Porridge
description: Nutritious alternative to maize porridge. Rich in iron and can be fortified with milk or groundnut paste.

name: Avocado
description: Excellent source of healthy fats and energy. Can be mashed and mixed with other foods. Widely grown in Rwanda.

name: Cassava
description: Good source of energy. Should be properly prepared and combined with protein-rich foods for balanced nutrition.

name: Small Fish
description: Small dried fish from Lake Kivu. Rich in calcium when eaten whole. Can be ground into powder and added to porridge.

name: Pumpkin
description: Rich in vitamin A and energy. Can be boiled and mashed. Pumpkin leaves are also nutritious.

name: Soybean
description: High-quality plant protein. Soy flour can be mixed with cereal flour to make enriched porridge.

name: Breast Milk
description: The ideal food for infants. Exclusive breastfeeding recommended for the first 6 months, continuing alongside complementary foods until age 2.
